hints: Look closely at the central carbon (the C in the middle) in the diagram and spot the four different groups attached to it.
Remember every amino acid has the same three groups (NH2, COOH and H) on that central carbon, so the R group must be the fourth, different side chain.
walkthrough:
**Recall the general amino acid structure**

Every amino acid has the same basic plan. A central carbon atom, called the alpha carbon, always holds three identical groups.

Those three are: an amino group ($NH_2$), a carboxyl group ($COOH$) and a hydrogen atom ($H$).

**Find those three on the diagram**

Look at the central C in glutamic acid. At the top is $COOH$, at the bottom is $NH_2$, and on the left is $H$.

That leaves only one arm left on the right side.

**Identify the R group**

The remaining arm on the right is $CH_2-CH_2-COOH$. This is the variable side chain that makes glutamic acid different from all other amino acids.

So the R group is $CH_2-CH_2-COOH$.

options.A: NH2 is the amino group found on every amino acid, not the variable R group.
options.B: H is the hydrogen atom found on every amino acid, not the variable R group.
options.C: COOH at the top is the carboxyl group found on every amino acid, not the whole R group (the R group just ends in a second COOH).
options.D: This is the unique side chain attached to the central carbon, so it is the R group for glutamic acid.
